101.lead: To be real with you — I don't do any of this out of pure passion. My process is a battle. With the brief, the obvious, and whatever comes too easy. That restlessness — that's where everything I do comes from. Design, leadership, coaching. All of it.
small: Under the performance, the noise, and the safe choices — there's something worth finding. When those layers finally break, the real and beautiful comes alive.
The brief doesn't own the outcome. The work answers to your vision — and comes out MF-stamped.
Having fun drawing rectangles or giving ten tips for a better life might work for some. But if you just need something raw, let's talk.
101.note: MY WORDS, NOT AI. BEEN EM-DASHING SINCE BEFORE IT WAS A RED FLAG.

heresy: Some designers are obsessed with spacing tokens, naming conventions, the newest plugin and the correct Figma structure — but strip away the software and the math and there is nothing left. Precision isn’t creativity.
Most persona decks aren’t discovery. They’re theater used to justify a decision someone already made. Watch behavior over stated preference.
If you can’t separate the work from your ego, every piece of feedback lands like an attack instead of information.
Most Designers Choose the Direction They Can Already Execute
Almost nobody picks the direction that might fail. Nobody sits in ‘I don’t know what this looks like yet’ long enough to find something.
Everyone hides behind the brief, the data or the client. Somewhere along the way, taste turned into a liability instead of the actual skill.
The process that was supposed to make designers better can become the thing keeping them stuck.
Critique isn’t a creative skill. It’s a verbal one. Don’t confuse the two.
Ten Years Doesn’t Make You Senior
A lot of seniors got there by sticking around, not by getting better.
Immediate answers optimize for looking good in the room. A real process optimizes for the work being right.
